newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: France, Germany vital to EMU - Dutch central banker.
newsitem.headline: France, Germany vital to EMU - Dutch central banker.

text.p: France and Germany must be among the countries which launch Economic and Monetary Union in 1999, but they must also meet the strict EMU entry conditions, the next president of the Dutch central bank said on Wednesday.

"In order to give sufficient weight to this core group, the participation of France and Germany -- forming as they do the axis of Western European cooperation -- is a prerequisite," Arnout Wellink, currently a central bank director, said in a speech delivered in Rotterdam.
"But with a view to the credibility of EMU, France and Germany in particular have to strictly observe the conditions of accession," Wellink said.

Speculation about which countries would take part in the launch of EMU was unproductive, he said, adding that all countries should instead do their utmost to achieve sustainable budgetary consolidation without resorting to tricks.

Wellink is due to succeed Wim Duisenberg as president of the central bank in June, when Duisenberg is due to take over as head of the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner of the European Central Bank.
The text of his speech was released to news media ahead of delivery.
